about.title: Clear legal guidance, in your language
paragraphs: Costa Legal is a bilingual law firm in Escazú that helps foreigners and Costa Ricans navigate Costa Rican law, from residency applications to property purchases, companies and insurance.
Costa Rica's systems are notoriously complex. We prepare the paperwork, deal with the institutions and keep you informed at every stage, so you can focus on your plans.
points: Personal attention from start to finish
Forms and filings prepared for you
A network of trusted realtors, developers and banks

items.q: How long does the residency process take?
items.a: There are three stages: about 8 weeks to gather documents, typically 9 to 12 months for the immigration department (DGME) to review your application, and about 4 weeks for your CCSS registration and DIMEX card. Times depend on the government's workload.

items.q: Can I stay in Costa Rica while my application is pending?
items.a: Yes. Once your application is filed, the DGME issues a receipt that, together with your passport, works as valid ID, and the law allows you to remain in the country while the application is pending.

items.q: Do my documents need to be translated?
items.a: Yes. Documents in another language must be translated into Spanish, and foreign documents must be apostilled or legalized. Birth certificates and background checks must be issued within six months before filing.

items.q: Can we start while I'm still abroad?
items.a: Yes. The first stage is gathering the documents you'll bring to Costa Rica, and we guide you through it wherever you are.
Yes. Our team works in English and Spanish, and we explain every document and step in the language you prefer.

hero.title: Make Costa Rica your home, legally
hero.intro: Costa Rica offers residency options for retirees, people with a stable income, investors, families and workers. We help you choose the right category and handle the process from start to finish.
hero.imageAlt: Passport and travel documents on a desk

categories.title: Find the right path
categories.intro: Each category has its own requirements. In your free consultation we confirm which one fits you.

items.title: Retirees
items.label: Pensionado
items.figure: Pension of at least $1,000 per month
items.text: For people receiving retirement income from their home country's social security or pension system. Disability income also qualifies, and your spouse and children can be included.

items.title: Fixed income
items.label: Rentista
items.text: Show a stable income, either by depositing $60,000 (two years of income) in a bank in Costa Rica or abroad, by certifying your income from abroad, or through a trust.

items.title: Investors
items.label: Inversionista
items.text: Invest in a Costa Rican business or in assets such as real estate.

items.title: Marriage to a Costa Rican
items.text: For foreign nationals married to a Costa Rican. After two years of marriage and residence in the country, you may apply for citizenship.

items.title: Parents of a Costa Rican
items.text: Foreign nationals with children born in Costa Rica are eligible for residency.

items.title: Self-employed & entrepreneurs
items.text: For people who want to work for themselves or run a business here. Skilled professionals can qualify based on their expertise, and owners of a physical business, such as a hotel or restaurant, have their own option.

items.title: Foreign workers
items.text: Costa Rican regulations offer several options for companies to hire foreign executives, managers, technicians and consultants. We help you find the right one.

requirements.title: General requirements
requirements.intro: Whatever the category, most applications include the following. Items marked "We handle it" are prepared by our team.

items.title: Proof of eligibility
items.text: Documents showing you qualify for your category, such as a pension letter for retirees, investment certifications for investors, or a Costa Rican marriage certificate.

items.title: Background check
items.text: Issued by a national authority in your home country: the FBI for US citizens, the RCMP for Canadians, or ACRO Criminal Records Office for UK nationals.

items.title: Birth certificate
items.text: A recently issued copy, no more than six months old.

items.title: Application form
items.text: Completed by our team.

items.title: Cover letter
items.text: A letter with your personal details for the application, prepared by us.

items.title: Fingerprints
items.text: Taken at a police station. We arrange the appointment in San José or Liberia, take you there from our office and handle the forms.

items.title: Certified passport copy
items.text: We certify your passport copy.

items.title: Consular registration
items.text: Registration with your country's consulate, completed by our team.

items.title: Passport photos
items.text: Passport-size photographs.

items.title: Government fees
items.text: $251 when you apply and $433 at the end of the process.

documents.title: About your documents
items: Documents in another language must be translated into Spanish. Translation costs vary by language.
Foreign documents must be authenticated: apostilled if your country is part of the Hague Apostille Convention, or legalized if it isn't.
Birth certificates, background checks and other foreign documents must be issued within six months before filing, so the original birth certificate from when you were born won't be accepted.
You need background checks from every country where you lived legally in the past three years. Time spent as a tourist doesn't count.

timeline.title: How long it takes
timeline.intro: A temporary residency application goes through three stages.

stages.title: Gathering documents
stages.text: We help you obtain the documents you'll bring to Costa Rica and prepare the rest of the application.

stages.title: DGME review and decision
stages.text: We file your application with the Dirección General de Migración y Extranjería (DGME). The law sets a 90-day limit, but processing currently takes much longer.

stages.title: Registration
stages.text: Once you're approved, we register you with the CCSS (Caja) and obtain your DIMEX residency card. This completes the process.

pending.title: While your application is pending
items: After filing, the DGME issues a receipt that, together with your passport, serves as valid ID.
You may stay in Costa Rica while your application is pending, without leaving every 90 days to renew your visa.

You can't get a Costa Rican driver's license until your DIMEX is issued. To keep driving on a foreign license, you must leave the country every 90 days to renew your entry stamp, a rule set by a different government department.
If you travel during the waiting period, you may be asked for a return ticket when you re-enter, by plane or by bus depending on how you arrive.
